correctness.rationale: The proof derives the actual unique ProxSPS minimizer using the original truncated loss and an unchanged ridge proximal term; the map has two continuous affine branches on a rigorously invariant interval. The branch ordering follows positive factorizations, the three orbit equalities hold identically, and the multiplier gives the exact local stability criterion. The Li–Yorke hypothesis of a continuous interval map with a genuine period-three point is met. The standalone exact-rational checker independently solves the convex subproblem at 10,112 sampled points; finite tests are corroborative only.

value.rationale: A finite, nontrivial structural obstruction to constant-large-step convergence for the actual ProxSPS algorithm is exhibited even with tight loss lower bounds and a globally strongly convex quadratic objective. A primitive, locally attracting three-cycle, its full open parameter domain, and the conditional all-period dynamical consequence materially distinguish the method from scalar gradient descent and standard SPS. These are motivated failure modes for an algorithm designed to stabilize composite stochastic optimization, not a mere routine stability factor.
